title: When UPGMA fails: the molecular clock

prompts.concept: This true tree is not clock-like: the branch to B is ten times the others, so B has drifted far from every other taxon. Watch where UPGMA goes wrong.
prompts.math: UPGMA joins the closest pair and sets each branch to d/2 — correct only when all tips are equally distant from the root (ultrametric).

prompts.concept: Because B races ahead, UPGMA's plain averages pull the wrong pair together first and the split it builds is not in the true tree.
prompts.math: Averaging distances assumes the cluster means stay comparable; a fast branch breaks that assumption.

prompts.concept: RF > 0: UPGMA built a different tree. Now switch the Method control to Neighbor-Joining — it corrects for unequal rates and should reach RF = 0.
prompts.math: NJ subtracts each cluster's average divergence (the r values) before joining, so an accelerated branch no longer misleads the search.
